<subject>RE: Mona Price Indication</subject>
<body>
Dear Mark,

If we consider this from a Hamburg index perspective, how would it appear? I believe the client wants to set a floating price based on an index but is looking for some guidance on the appropriate basis relative to Hamburg. This isn’t a firm offer since there’s no actual transaction planned; it’s more of a market indication. It’s a bit unusual, but the more competitive our price is against Hamburg, the better our chances of securing the deal. We should present a strong indicative bid, subject to credit approval and other conditions. When it comes time to finalize, which is unlikely given the units’ lack of historical data, the market price could be quite different.

Best regards,  
Michael

-----Original Message-----  
From: Fischer, Mark  
Sent: Wednesday, June 20, 2001 09:32  
To: Etringer, Michael  
Cc: Alonso, Tom; Salisbury, Holden  
Subject: Mona Price Indication

Michael, here are the quarterly price indications for Mona as discussed:

     Q3 2021  Q4 2021  Q1 2022  Q2 2022

Peak  120    65    50    49

Off-peak 57    38    30    28

The prices indicated are for firm power delivery with liquidated damages. Products contingent on unit availability will be discounted by 20%-30% on peak and 10%-20% on off-peak depending on the contract term.
</body>
